title: North India cotton yarn steadies, close watch on ceasefire deal
summary:
North India’s cotton yarn market remained weak due to sluggish downstream demand despite easing labour shortages.
Traders are monitoring the proposed US-Iran ceasefire, which could lower energy and polyester feedstock costs and support textile activity.
However, buyers remain cautious, while recycled yarn demand and cotton trade sentiment continue to stay subdued.

title: UK's Frasers targets full takeover of Accent Group
summary:
Frasers Group has launched an all-cash takeover offer to acquire the Accent Group shares it does not already own, valuing the deal at about £166 million (~$222.5 million). 
The UK retailer, which holds a 22.9 per cent stake in Accent, is offering A$0.65 per share. 
The unconditional offer will run from June 30 to July 30, 2026, subject to any extension or withdrawal.

title: Sustainable cotton shock: India leads sell-off on duty waiver
summary:
Certified cotton prices weakened across key markets, led by India, where duty-free cotton imports and proposed US tariffs triggered sharp declines in BCI and organic cotton. 
China also softened on weaker yarn demand, while Pakistan remained unchanged. 
The market is increasingly being driven by policy developments and demand concerns rather than crop fundamentals.

title: Global container freight analysis: Major ports in H1 2026
summary:
Global freight rates rebounded sharply in H1 2026, driven by early peak-season demand, carrier capacity management and Middle East tensions. 
Asia-US routes recorded the strongest gains, while Red Sea disruptions and higher fuel costs supported rates. 
For textile exporters, logistics costs increased, though better vessel availability and schedule reliability helped maintain supply chain stability.

title: Oil prices slide; Indian refiners' and textile stocks rise
summary:
Crude oil prices slumped on June 15 as easing US-Iran tensions reduced fears of supply disruptions, pushing Brent and WTI down by over 5 per cent. 
The decline lifted Indian refining, LNG and textile stocks as investors anticipated lower feedstock and energy costs. 
Sustained weakness in crude could improve refining margins, reduce synthetic fibre costs, ease inflation and support corporate earnings.

title: FESPA 2026 sees higher turnout & stronger investment
summary:
FESPA 2026 drew 24,798 visitors from 126 countries, with unique attendance rising 10 per cent year on year. 
The event expanded with new Textile and Corrugated showcases alongside existing exhibitions and conferences, reinforcing its role as a global hub for innovation, investment and business growth across speciality print and related sectors.

title: BCI terms FY27 Bangladesh budget proposals ‘reform-oriented’
summary:
Terming the proposed FY27 national budget as ‘reform-oriented’ and ‘business-friendly’ that could help revive economic activities amid prevailing domestic and global challenges, the Bangladesh Chamber of Industries has praised introduction of structural reform measures in key areas. 
It also hailed the government's emphasis on developing ten priority sectors, the creative economy and the blue economy.

title: Indian textile industry sees respite from expected US-Iran peace deal
summary:
India’s textile and apparel industry expects the proposed US-Iran deal to ease trade and supply-chain pressures by improving shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and supporting lower crude oil prices.
Industry stakeholders believe the agreement could reduce raw material and energy costs, strengthen export competitiveness and create a more stable environment for global textile trade.

title: D BADAMI Fashion Connection to display shirting fabrics at Bharat Tex
summary:
D BADAMI Fashion Connection LLP will showcase its premium men's shirting fabric portfolio at Bharat Tex 2026 in New Delhi from July 14-17. 
Exhibiting at Stall 5G-K5, the company will highlight innovative woven fabrics across multiple fibre blends and constructions. 
It aims to expand its domestic and global presence while advancing technology-driven fabric sourcing and design solutions.

title: India, France call for early implementation of India-EU FTA
summary:
Indian PM Narendra Modi and French President Emmanuel Macron called for early implementation of the India-EU FTA as both leaders met yesterday in Nice.
This was their first meeting since the elevation of bilateral ties to ‘Special Global Strategic Partnership’ earlier this year. 
Both agreed to set up a high-level mechanism to double bilateral trade within five years and strengthen supply chain resilience.

title: Bangladesh-US apparel paradox shows higher rank and weaker momentum
summary:
Bangladesh remains the second-largest apparel supplier to the US, but exports are losing momentum despite China’s sharp decline.
Falling shipment value, volume and unit prices indicate growing competitive pressure.
To capture more market share, Bangladesh must strengthen synthetic fibre capabilities, speed, flexibility and compliance rather than relying solely on low-cost manufacturing.

title: US apparel sourcing shifts beyond Asia Americas in 2.6 bn third map
summary:
US apparel sourcing is becoming more diversified as buyers reduce dependence on traditional suppliers. 
While Asia remains dominant, Europe, Africa and the Middle East are gaining share due to their strengths in quality, traceability, compliance and risk management. 
Future sourcing decisions will increasingly balance cost, speed, resilience and regulatory certainty.

title: US textile & apparel imports volume down 10.6% in Jan-Apr 2026
summary:
US textile and apparel imports fell 10.68 per cent year on year to 29.39 billion SME in January–April 2026, with apparel imports down 12.82 per cent and textiles down 9.94 per cent.
Cotton and MMF imports also declined.
Exports dropped 7.72 per cent, reflecting weaker trade activity, although apparel exports recorded growth, highlighting uneven demand across segments.

title: US T&A exports drop 9% in January-April 2026 amid soft demand
summary:
US textile and apparel exports fell 9.36 per cent to $6.85 billion in January-April 2026, reflecting weaker demand across regional supply chains.
Yarn exports saw the steepest decline, indicating slower upstream activity, while shipments to key markets such as Mexico, Honduras and China contracted sharply.
The trend points to cautious sourcing and softer manufacturing momentum.

title: Poland’s LPP posts strong Q1 as profit jumps 42%
summary:
Poland’s LPP has reported strong Q1 2026 results, with revenue rising 11 per cent YoY to PLN 5.5 billion (~$1.485 billion) and net profit increasing 42 per cent. 
EBITDA grew 36 per cent to PLN 1.3 billion (~$351 million), supported by a record 58.5 per cent gross margin and cost discipline. 
The retailer opened 121 stores, led by Sinsay, while investing in retail expansion and logistics infrastructure.

title: China compliance wall raises proof over production in apparel sourcing
summary:
China’s 2026 compliance decrees are reshaping apparel sourcing by making supply-chain data harder to collect and transfer. 
As global traceability demands rise, competitive advantage will shift from low-cost production to verifiable proof of origin, labour and supplier links. 
China remains central to textile supply chains, making transparency (not relocation) the key sourcing challenge.

title: Bangladesh-Japan EPA opens $3 bn apparel export door with RMG push
summary:
Bangladesh aims to raise apparel exports to Japan from about $1.3-1.4 billion to $3 billion, requiring monthly shipments to roughly double. 
The 2026 EPA secures duty-free access and flexible rules of origin, boosting competitiveness. 
Success will depend on converting buyer interest into repeat orders through stronger quality, compliance, sourcing and Japan-focused execution.

title: US' Oxford Industries' Q1 sales slip 0.4% amid tariffs
summary:
Oxford Industries has reported Q1 net sales of $391 million, broadly flat YoY, while adjusted EPS declined to $1.39 due to $11 million in additional tariff costs. 
Tommy Bahama delivered growth, but Lilly Pulitzer and Johnny Was sales weakened. 
The company narrowed its FY26 sales outlook to $1.475-1.505 billion while maintaining confidence that lower tariffs.

title: Cambodia garment exports maintain growth despite May slowdown
summary:
Cambodia’s apparel exports rose 5.6 per cent YoY to $4.45 billion in January-May 2026, accounting for 31.7 per cent of total exports.
Growth was driven by both knitted and woven garments, although May shipments declined 7.3 per cent.
Cotton and cotton yarn imports surged 27.1 per cent, signalling stronger demand for cotton-based apparel production.

title: Bangladesh exporters concerned over US tariff move under Section 301
summary:
The United States Trade Representative (USTR) has proposed 10–12.5 per cent tariffs on 60 countries, including Bangladesh, over forced-labour concerns after Section 301 findings. 
Exporters warn total US tariffs could reach ~44 per cent, hurting competitiveness.
Exporters are urging cooperation and capacity-building measures instead of punitive tariffs.
